questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Which policy is expansionary fiscal policy?
questions.explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy increases spending or cuts taxes to boost aggregate demand. Raising taxes is contractionary.
questions.hint: Expansionary means more spending or lower taxes.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Which policy is contractionary fiscal policy?
questions.explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy cuts spending or raises taxes to reduce aggregate demand. Cutting taxes is expansionary.
questions.hint: Contractionary means less spending or higher taxes.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Identify a shifter of aggregate demand

questions.explanation: Higher consumer confidence raises consumption, shifting aggregate demand right. The others reduce demand.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: MPC is 0.6; what is the spending multiplier?
questions.explanation: The multiplier is one divided by one minus 0.6, or 2.5. A lower MPC means a smaller multiplier.
questions.hint: Divide one by one minus MPC.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: MPC is 0.6; what is the tax multiplier?
questions.explanation: The tax multiplier is negative MPC over one minus MPC, or -1.5. Tax cuts raise GDP.
questions.hint: Use negative MPC over one minus MPC.

questions.explanation: Deficit borrowing competes for funds. Higher rates reduce private investment.
